caption:
Custom instructions are not a personality test.

Everyone tells you to fill in the "about me" box in ChatGPT like it's a dating profile. "I'm a curious person who loves learning." Cool. So is literally everyone using AI.

Here's what actually moves the needle:

→ Tell it how you process information first (big picture vs. details first)
→ Tell it what annoys you (bullet points? long disclaimers? being talked down to?)
→ Tell it what you're actually trying to DO most of the time
→ Tell it how you make decisions (gut + data? pure logic? consensus?)

For ChatGPT: Settings → Personalization → Custom Instructions. Two boxes. Most people fill one. Fill both.

For Claude: Start a new chat and literally say "here's how I think" before your first real question. Claude holds context better than you'd expect.

For Gemini: Use the Gems feature if you're on Advanced. Build a specific gem for your most repeated use case instead of trying to make one instruction set do everything.

The real problem isn't the platform. It's that you're describing yourself like a resume instead of describing how your brain actually works under pressure.

That's the gap bootfile.ai exists to close.
hook: Your custom instructions are doing nothing. Here's why.
